title: Zonneboiler en WaterAccu: een betere vergelijking
excerpt: Curious about a comparison between a solar water heater and a wateraccu? Read more in this blog and discover the differences.
contentHtml:
Do you not remember it all with all the sustainability options on the market? In this blog we take a closer look at two options for sustainable heating of tap water; namely the solar water heater and WaterAccu.

The best way for hot tap water

There are currently many options for making households more sustainable in many areas. Solar panels are so popular that buyers need less and less support to make them profitable, and (hybrid) heat pumps are also increasingly becoming the norm. Also for a single subject in sustainable, warm tap water, there are options from smartboilers to quookers, heat pump boilers, and of course the WaterAccu from Solyx.

In a previous blog (Optimization of use of solar energy: an overview), the WaterAccu has already been compared with other options to see what best suits different situations. There is one technology that does cause some confusion with the WaterAccu, namely the solar water heater. This technology also uses solar energy as much as possible to heat tap water. To clarify this confusion, this blog will perform an additional comparison between a solar water heater and the WaterAccu.

How does a solar water heater work?

A solar water heater works as a system independent of other technologies in the home. It consists of a buffer tank, a heat exchanger, and a solar collector with pipes containing a special liquid. The buffer tank contains the tap water. The solar collector is placed on the roof to absorb sunlight. No power is then produced, but the liquid in the collector is heated by the heat of the sun. This liquid then flows through a pumping system to the buffer tank, and the tap water is heated via the heat exchanger. The cooled liquid is then pumped back to the collector to be reheated. The buffer tank may be linked to a source for extra heating, for example the central heating combination boiler. This is necessary on days with little sunlight.

How does the WaterAccu work?

The WaterAccu is intended for households with solar panels with a lot of surplus. The system consists of an electric boiler and the Solar iBoost, the smart box that works as a control device. The Solar iBoost comes standard with a transmitter and a measuring clamp. When installed, the Solar iBoost is connected to the electric boiler and the measuring clamp is placed in the meter box at the phase where solar power is supplied. When the solar panels produce power, it is first used by devices at the same stage. Unused power is supplied to the grid. However, the clamp measures when this happens, and gives the iBoost a signal that power is available. The electric boiler is then controlled to heat, so that the power can still be used. Optionally, the boiler can also be connected in series with a CV combination boiler so that tap water is additionally heated on days with little sunlight.

What is the best choice for different scenarios?

Although the solar water heater and WaterAccu providing the same function, there are clear differences. The solar water heater uses its own source of energy that cannot be used by other devices in the house. However, space is needed for the collector, which can be difficult for houses that already have solar panels. In addition, some households will have to choose to install either a solar water heater or solar panels, and solar panels will be more useful.

The WaterAccu is less independent than the solar water heater, but is easier to install and gives extra value to existing solar panels. In addition, the WaterAccu also has the option of heating extra with power from the grid, while the solar boiler for extra heating must be connected to another device.

Ultimately, the WaterAccu is aimed at making better use of solar power by heating tap water, and the solar water heater is fully focused on heating tap water. Both options therefore make sustainability more sustainable. If you do not have solar panels, a solar water heater will help to reduce gas consumption, and if you do have solar panels, the WaterAccu can improve your own use of solar power, while also reducing gas costs.

Read more about the Solar iBoost, the control device of the WaterAccu
